items.q: A client needs WFI, stainless or a hot-held loop. What then?
items.a: We supply one ambient polypropylene Purified Water (PW) package with polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pretreatment. No Water for Injection (WFI), pure steam, stills or stainless steel systems. Steam, a hot-held loop or routine 80 °C at loop pressure needs a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) or stainless loop [whether we quote PVDF]. A standard requiring stainless rules out polypropylene, unless it allows exceptions.

items.q: Who will audit the water system?
items.a: Health Canada inspects under your establishment licence (GUI-0001); the FDA, when a client sells in the US. Each client's quality unit audits too, routinely and for cause. Natural health product sites follow GUI-0158 under their site licence.

items.q: Who owns the water data, us or our clients?
items.a: Usually you: the water system is a site utility. Each quality agreement sets what that client receives (GUI-0001 C.02.012). Per-client reports: [reporting by suite, outlet and date].

items.q: Can you attend our clients' audits?
items.a: Your clients audit the water system as part of your site. Our attendance as your supplier, in person or by video: [client audit attendance and terms].

items.q: Our clients will ask about you. What can we show them?
items.a: Your clients can question the engineer who would lead your project and receive a written answer. They can audit our quality system on [on-site audit notice, working days] notice. They can witness the factory acceptance test (FAT) and read our specimen documents. Each check gives them a record to file.

items.q: Our system is another maker's, with paper records. Where do we start?
items.a: For [makes and equipment types serviced]: with a system assessment of drawings, qualification file, trends and data integrity against your clients' markets.
